USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

monteggia — clinical decision 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

During treatment of a Monteggia injury, the surgeon confirms anatomical reduction and stable fixation of the ulna. The radial head nevertheless remains irreducible with appropriate gentle maneuvers. Which explanation should guide further exploration of the proximal joint?

  1. Interposed annular ligament or other soft tissue
  2. Residual ulnar shortening
  3. Residual ulnar angular deformity
  4. An isolated tear of the triangular fibrocartilage complex
  5. An isolated collateral ligament sprain without interposition
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Interposed annular ligament or other soft tissue

A soft-tissue block can prevent radial head reduction after the bony alignment has been corrected.

Understanding the options

Interposed annular ligament or other soft tissue
A soft-tissue block can prevent radial head reduction after the bony alignment has been corrected.
Residual ulnar shortening
The case specifies that ulnar length and alignment have been restored anatomically.
Residual ulnar angular deformity
Anatomical ulnar reduction has already been confirmed.
An isolated tear of the triangular fibrocartilage complex
The TFCC is distal and does not mechanically block the radial head.
An isolated collateral ligament sprain without interposition
A sprain may affect stability but does not by itself explain a mechanical block to reduction.
